basis_statement: Identifiers remain schema-permitted strings with lightweight branding so IDs, refs, hashes, and route tokens cannot drift into one undifferentiated string bag.

source_lineage.source_heading_or_logical_block: object-family naming patterns and canonical field suffixes
source_lineage.rationale: The corpus standardizes *_id, *_ref, *_hash, and route-token usage across artifacts.

source_lineage.source_heading_or_logical_block: deterministic serialization and replay-safe runtime conventions
source_lineage.rationale: Primitive helpers must preserve lawful values rather than add ad hoc narrowing.
Identifier families need stable distinctions at service, API, worker, and viewer seams.

identifier_families.label: Identifiers
identifier_families.summary: Opaque entity identifiers keep family meaning without regex invention.
notes: Do not impose slug-only or UUID-only assumptions unless a specific schema requires them.
Identifiers stay serializable as plain strings at contract boundaries.

example_fields.note: Punctuation remains lawful because the helper only rejects empty or non-string input.
Command IDs remain opaque replay keys rather than parsed routing strings.

forbidden_shortcuts: Do not coerce numbers into identifier strings.
Do not add family-specific regexes inside the shared primitive layer.

identifier_families.label: References
identifier_families.summary: References point to external or cross-artifact linkage without collapsing into IDs.
notes: Refs often carry lineage or locator meaning and must stay distinguishable from entity IDs.
Schema families may permit provider-flavored values that the shared layer must not over-constrain.

example_fields.note: Freeze references remain opaque execution-basis locators.
Lineage refs can contain path-like tokens and still remain lawful.

forbidden_shortcuts: Do not strip separators from refs for cosmetic normalization.
Do not assume refs can be used interchangeably with IDs.

identifier_families.label: Hashes
identifier_families.summary: Digest strings keep hash meaning explicit at replay, release, and policy boundaries.
notes: Hash branding distinguishes digest artifacts from plain refs or IDs even though the wire type remains string.
The shared layer does not assume a prefix like sha256: unless a contract says so.

example_fields.note: Digest values remain lowercase hex under the canonical hash profile.
Some contracts retain provider-specific prefixes and the helper must not reject them.

forbidden_shortcuts: Do not derive digests from locale-formatted or whitespace-rich stringification.
Do not treat any non-empty hash string as proof of canonicality without using the hash helpers.

identifier_families.label: Route Tokens
identifier_families.summary: Route tokens are browser-visible locators and must not be confused with IDs or mutable labels.
notes: Route tokens remain legal strings because atlas and shell routes are path-bearing by design.
The shared layer brands them without claiming ownership of router-specific parsing.

example_fields.note: Preview locators remain route tokens rather than identifiers.

forbidden_shortcuts: Do not derive authority from breadcrumbs or human labels.
Do not normalize away routing punctuation that a router or storage boundary preserves.
